title: HostedAPI deferred ACK wavefront afteraction
content:
Summary:

On 2026-11-07 ~02:18 UTC we observed a large wave of deferred ACKs from edge proxies into the Hosted API streaming path. The symptom was a multi-minute p99 TTFB spike and an elevated 5xx rate (~1.6% system-wide for the streaming front) for ~7 minutes, followed by a slower tail of increased latency and partial streaming fragmentation for ~22 minutes. The incident was P0 (affecting many tenants with streaming sessions) and triggered on-call escalation.

High-level impact:
- p99 TTFB for streaming endpoints jumped from baseline ~280ms to ~3.1s at peak.
- Successful streaming session completions dropped ~11% for the active 30-minute window.
- Customer-facing errors: increased 502/503 for streaming handoff path; ~400 requests failed with explicit client-side reconnect.
- No data loss at model layer; most requests eventually completed after retries.

Timeline (reconstructed from traces and heartbeats):
- 02:17:58 UTC: first heartbeats from edge proxies show increased send queues.
- 02:18:10 UTC: internal alert - streaming p99 TTFB > 1200ms for 3 minutes. Pager triggered.
- 02:18:45 UTC: on-call SRE (Jonas) begins triage: looks at acceptor/backlog, ephemeral queue lengths, and edge metrics.
- 02:19:40 UTC: first spike of deferred ACKs observed in edge tracing (many ACK events queued behind retransmit throttles).
- 02:20:10 UTC: engineering (serving-runtime) looped in to check multiplexer and mux-hedging logic.
- 02:23:00 UTC: mitigation 1 - raised the acceptor backpressure threshold for the edge fleet (temporary knob) to allow inflight queue to drain.
- 02:25:30 UTC: p99 declines slightly but fragmentation still present.
- 02:27:00 UTC: mitigation 2 - applied a conservative rollback of a recent edge rate-limiter tweak (github PR referenced below).
- 02:29:00 UTC: bulk deferred-ACK wave subsides; streaming p99 returns toward baseline by ~02:32 UTC.
- 02:55:00 UTC: residual churning and reconnects slow down; follow-up tasks created.

Root cause (summary):
Primary root cause was an interaction between a recent change to the edge ACK pacing (PR 1287) and unusual fanout patterns from a downstream customer workload. The change introduced a slightly more aggressive in-order ACK batching heuristic that, under high multiplexing and asymmetric retransmit backpressure, caused sizable ACK waves that arrived at the hosting layer in bursts. Those bursts synchronized across many edge shards and overloaded the streaming connection acceptor and per-tenant request windows, creating queuing that manifested as p99 TTFB spikes and transient 5xx failures.

Contributing factors:
- PR 1287 lowered ACK emission granularity to reduce small-packet overhead; this increased coalescing in some conditions.
- A downstream client (identified - tenant-78) executed a sudden pattern with many concurrent long-lived streaming sessions that biased sequence numbers and kept many connections warm simultaneously; this created conditions for ACK waves.
- Acceptors had a conservative queue-threshold setting (hysteresis) tuned for steady-state load and not for short synchronized bursts.
- We lacked a clear circuit-breaker that would back off hedging/fanout when inbound ACK waveforms exceed expected variance.
- Telemetry: the existing dashboards showed p99 TTFB, error counts, and some ack-rate metrics, but the specific time-series for ACK batching size and inter-ack interval distribution were not exposed at the level needed for rapid triage.

Immediate mitigations taken during the incident:
- Temporarily relaxed acceptor backpressure thresholds across the edge fleet to allow bursty ACK arrival to be absorbed. (Action: SRE oncall, Jonas)
- Rolled back the most recent ACK pacing heuristic to previous behavior for the edge release (serving-runtime / Marco). Rollback was deployed to canary then fleet-wide within ~8 minutes.
- Rate-limited the tenant identified as highest fanout (tenant-78) for 10 minutes to reduce reinforcing feedback while systems recovered (Customer Success notified).
- Increased tracing sampling for ACK events and connection acceptor spans for 2 hours to capture richer telemetry for postmortem.

Why rollbacks/threshold changes were safe: the acceptor change was a temporary operational knob with limited blast radius (edge-only) and system health checks were monitored during rollout. The ACK pacing rollback was low-risk because it returned behavior to a tested baseline.

Longer-term fixes and action items (owners and ETA):
1) Telemetry: add per-edge-series metrics: ack_batched_size_histogram, inter_ack_interval_p99, per-shard ack-burst-rate. (Owner: Leah; ETA: 2026-11-21)
2) Controller: implement an ACK-wave detector that temporarily disables aggressive coalescing once inter-ack intervals show burstiness beyond threshold. (Owner: Marco; ETA: 2026-12-05)
3) Acceptors: introduce a fast-path circuit-breaker that drops or rejects new streaming fanout when internal queue growth rate > X/s for > Y seconds. Add a slow-gro recovery mode. (Owner: Ravi; ETA: 2026-12-10)
4) Release process: add a post-deploy smoke check that simulates short high-fanout streaming pattern to validate ACK/coalescing behavior. (Owner: Aisha; ETA: 2026-11-18)
5) Documentation / runbook: update the streaming incident runbook with new playbook steps to identify ACK-wave signatures and recommended knobs (acceptor-threshold, ack-coalesce-toggle, tenant-rate-limit). (Owner: Jonas; ETA: 2026-11-14)
6) Customer outreach: CS to follow up with tenant-78 and share mitigation steps + recommended SDK best-practices to avoid synchronized reconnect waves. (Owner: Leah (CS coord); ETA: 2026-11-12)

Runbook additions (draft checklist to include):
- Alert triage: for streaming p99 spikes, immediately query ack_interarrival_rate and ack_batched_size in last 5m. If ack_batched_size p90 > baseline*3, label "ack-wave".
- If ack-wave labeled: 1) raise acceptor queue threshold by +25% temporarily, 2) toggle ack-coalesce flag on canary edge nodes, 3) identify top 3 tenants by concurrent streaming sessions and apply soft rate-limit if one tenant accounts for >40% of concurrent sessions.
- If 5xx rate > 0.5% coupled with ack-wave, engage serving-runtime and apply immediate rollback of last ACK-related change (if within 24h).
- Post-incident: increase tracing sampling to 100% for ACK spans for 1 hr and collect packet-level traces if available.

Monitoring queries / quick checks for oncall:
- streaming.p99_ttfb[5m] by region/shard
- edge.ack.batched_size.p90[5m] by shard
- edge.ack.interarrival.p99[5m] by shard
- acceptor.queue_growth_rate[1m]
- streaming.connection_fail_rate[5m]
- top_concurrent_streams_by_tenant[5m]

Operational notes (lessons learned):
- Micro-optimizations that change batching/coalescing heuristics can produce emergent system-level behavior when synchronized across many shards. We need a safer rollout plan for these classes of changes (simulated fanout tests + extended canary observation windows).
- Telemetry blind spots cost precious minutes during triage. We must instrument ack cadence and batching size by default for streaming edge releases.
- Playbook should prioritize identifying whether the spike is inbound (client-driven) vs. node-driven (release/regression). The mitigations differ (tenant throttle vs. rollback).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- What exact tenant SDK behavior triggered the synchronized ACK pattern? Need CS + SDK team to replay logs and client patterns. (Assigned to Leah)
- Should we build per-tenant ACK emit budgets to prevent single tenants from dominating aggregator queues? (Discuss on 2026-11-16 design review)
- Is there correlation with network-level retransmit/backoff on specific POPs? Need packet-level pcap sampling on affected shards; SRE infra to schedule.

Post-incident comms plan:
- Internal: short incident digest to #sre and #serving-runtime summarizing root cause and immediate mitigations. (Drafted by Aisha; send by 2026-11-10 EOD)
- External: CS outreach to affected large tenants with a summary and recommended SDK patterns; public status page entry for the 2026-11-07 incident with high-level user impact (prepared by Leah; ETA 2026-11-11).

Appendix: quick reproducibility notes (for devs)
- Repro pattern: spawn ~200 concurrent streaming sessions from a single client IP (tenant-78-like) with staggered start windows of 50ms and use SDK with keepalive probes every 6s. Watch ack coalescing; verify ack_batched_size histogram shifts.
- Local mitigation test: flip ack_coalesce boolean in canary and run the above load; monitor acceptor.queue_growth_rate.

Action tracker (short):
- Aisha: finalize incident digest and send internal comms (ETA 2026-11-10)
- Leah: CS follow-up with tenant-78 + reproduce logs (ETA 2026-11-12)
- Marco: design ACK-wave detector and begin spike detection prototype (ETA 2026-11-21)
- Ravi: implement acceptor circuit-breaker spec and initial PR (ETA 2026-12-03)
- Jonas: update runbook and add monitoring queries to the incident dashboard (ETA 2026-11-14)

Notes to future oncall: if you see a sudden multi-shard synchronized p99 spike for streaming with ack-batched-size increasing, do NOT immediately scale up model serving; first check ack-wave signature and consider toggling ack_coalesce/acceptor thresholds. Scaling model capacity without addressing ACK-wave will likely worsen queueing and hide the real problem.

Recorded artifacts and diagnostics collected: higher-sample traces, acceptor queue histograms, edge backpressure events, and full deployment timeline for PR 1287. Artifacts linked above.

Document history: initial draft 2026-11-07 (post-incident notes), updated with root-cause artifacts and action assignments 2026-11-10.
